slides.texte_overlay:
How to feel calmer around
people when you're anxious
Get there a little early. Walking into a quiet room is much easier than walking into a full one. People who arrive later come to you.
Give yourself a small role. Help with drinks, take photos, set up the music. Having a task makes social situations feel less pressured.
Bring a friend you feel safe with. One familiar face can calm your whole body. Over time, you'll need them less and less.
Lower your expectations. You don't need to be the funniest or the most interesting. Just being friendly is more than enough.
Before: I didn't know what to talk about. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having stories makes me feel much calmer.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I didn't know what to talk about. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having stories makes me feel much calmer.

slides.texte_overlay: Take a break when you need one. Step outside, get some air, come back. Leaving for five minutes is better than leaving for good.
Celebrate going, not just how it went. Every time you show up, your brain learns that social situations are safe. That's real progress.
